title: Vacation rental maintenance issues by season: what 150,000 tasks show
summary: What breaks at vacation rentals and when: 150,311 tasks by category and season, and a seasonal preventive maintenance calendar to copy.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**General maintenance is the biggest category of vacation rental issues, but the mix shifts with the seasons. In 150,311 unscheduled tasks logged at rental businesses over 12 months, heating and cooling, pest and outdoor problems all take a bigger share in summer, plumbing stays steady all year, and pool and hot tub issues peak in spring. More than half of all tasks were created by AI, mostly from a guest message or review, not typed by a person.**


## Key takeaways


- **The top five issue categories:** general maintenance ( **17%** of unscheduled tasks), guest requests ( **14%** ), early check-in requests ( **11%** ), cleanliness ( **8%** ) and access problems ( **8%** ).
- **Plumbing is the most common specific repair** , at **4%** of all unscheduled tasks and **10 to 13%** of repair tasks in every season.
- **Summer shifts the mix.** Heating and cooling goes from **5.4%** of repair tasks in spring to **9.2%** in summer; pest control from **3.9%** to **5.9%** .
- **Pool and hot tub issues peak in spring** at **9.4%** of repair tasks, as pools reopen.
- **Most tasks start in the inbox.** **58%** of all tasks were created by AI (nine in ten of those from a guest message or review), **30%** came from recurring or booking-triggered schedules, and **10%** were typed by a person.

## Where we're coming from


I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and we host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree, three places with very different seasons. When we plan preventive work, the question is always the same: what is about to break, and where? Here's what a year of maintenance tasks says.


> **How we measured it.** Tasks created in ProhostAI from November 1, 2025 to November 1, 2026, excluding deleted tasks and internal or test workspaces: 216,915 tasks. "Unscheduled" tasks are everything except recurring and booking-triggered schedules and automated system alerts: 150,311 tasks at 695 businesses, each tied to a listing. Categories are the ones on each task, set by the AI or by the host. Seasons use the listing's local month and include only northern-hemisphere listings, so July is summer everywhere in the seasonal tables. Customer growth means raw monthly counts rise all year, so we compare each season's mix (the share of repair tasks in each category) rather than raw counts. Every number we publish has at least 5 businesses and 30 listings behind it.

The rest are smaller categories and custom ones. Two things are worth noticing. First, more than a third of the list isn't repairs at all: guest requests, early check-in, late checkout and booking help are guests asking for something. Second, access problems (codes, locks, keys) are as common as cleanliness problems. They're also the issue that most often[brings a call at night](https://prohost.ai/blog/what-guests-call-about-at-night) .

What the seasons say:


- **Heating and cooling has two peaks.** It's highest in summer (air conditioning) and second-highest in winter (heat), and quietest in spring. Service AC before June and heat before December, not when the first guest complains.
- **Pests come with the heat.** Pest tasks take their biggest share in summer and stay elevated into fall.
- **Pools and hot tubs peak in spring.** That's when pools reopen and heaters, pumps and chemistry get tested by the first guests of the year.
- **Plumbing never takes a season off.** It's 10 to 13% of repairs all year. Slow drains, running toilets and water heaters are steady work.
- **Outdoor and utility issues build through summer and fall** , with storms, yard work and outdoor furniture.


We also checked the same 23 businesses in both winter and summer (608 listings). Per 100 checkouts, their repair tasks rose from **27 in winter to 31 in summer** , and pool and hot tub tasks nearly doubled. One business makes up a large share of that group's winter tasks, so treat it as directional.


## Your seasonal maintenance calendar (copy this)


**Late winter (February)**


- Service pool and hot tub heaters, pumps and covers before spring bookings.
- Test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; replace batteries.
- Check for winter leaks under sinks and around water heaters.


**Spring (March to May)**


- Service air conditioning: filters, coils, condensate lines, thermostats.
- Book pest control before the first warm month.
- Check outdoor furniture, grills, fire pits and lighting.


**Summer (June to August)**


- Change AC filters monthly at busy properties.
- Check Wi-Fi equipment and speeds; summer brings more guests working from the rental.
- Inspect hot tub water and covers weekly.


**Fall (September to November)**


- Service heating: furnace filters, heat pumps, fireplaces and chimneys.
- Clean gutters and check exterior lighting before the dark months.
- Insulate exposed pipes where it freezes.


**Every turnover, all year**


- Run every faucet, flush every toilet, test the hot water.
- Test the door code and the backup way in.
- Note anything slow, loose or noisy so it becomes a task before it becomes a review.

## FAQ


### What are the most common vacation rental maintenance issues?


In our data, general maintenance was the largest category (17.5% of unscheduled tasks), followed by guest requests, early check-in requests, cleanliness and access problems. Among specific repairs, plumbing was the most common.


### When do short-term rental maintenance issues peak?


Heating and cooling issues take their largest share of repairs in summer and their second-largest in winter. Pest control peaks in summer, and pool and hot tub issues peak in spring.


### How many maintenance tasks should I expect per stay?


At 23 businesses we tracked through both seasons, repair tasks ran about 27 per 100 checkouts in winter and 31 per 100 in summer. Your number depends heavily on the age of the property and its amenities.


### How do I prevent maintenance issues at my rental?


Service heating and cooling before each peak season, book pest control before the first warm month, test every fixture and the door code at each turnover, and turn small notes from cleaners into tasks before they become guest complaints.


## The takeaway


Most rental maintenance is predictable. Plumbing is steady, heat and AC follow the thermometer, pools wake up in spring and pests arrive with summer. A calendar that services each system before its season, plus a habit of turning every guest complaint into a task, covers most of what breaks.
